Jorge Isaacs, María, translated by Rollo Ogden.
Standard Ebooks edition: https://standardebooks.org/ebooks/jorge-isaacs/maria/rollo-ogden

People whose words are in the text, and their death years:
- Jorge Isaacs, the author, died 1895.
- Rollo Ogden, the translator, died 1937.

First publication of the text used: 1890 (SE colophon: 'It was translated from Spanish in 1890 by Rollo Ogden.')

Why this is public domain:
- United States: the text was first published in 1890, before 1931, so it is in the public domain in the United States. The edition's rights statement below says the same.
- Country of origin (not named in the facts; the translation is in English, so the possible countries are the United Kingdom, Ireland, the United States, Canada, Australia, New Zealand, India and South Africa): each has a copyright term of life plus 70 years or less. The last person to die, Rollo Ogden (died 1937), means the translation is public domain in each of them from 1 January 2008 at the latest. The original Spanish work by Jorge Isaacs is also public domain in every country, because its author died in 1925 or earlier.

The edition's own statement of rights (from the repository's content.opf):
"The source text and artwork in this ebook are believed to be in the United States public domain; that is, they are believed to be free of copyright restrictions in the United States. They may still be copyrighted in other countries, so users located outside of the United States must check their local laws before using this ebook. The creators of, and contributors to, this ebook dedicate their contributions to the worldwide public domain via the terms in the [CC0 1.0 Universal Public Domain Dedication](https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/)."

Sources of these facts:
- SE colophon: 'María was published in 1867 by Jorge Isaacs. It was translated from Spanish in 1890 by Rollo Ogden.'
- Wikidata Q1703852 (Jorge Isaacs), P570 = 1895-04-17.
- Wikidata Q16785357 (Rollo Ogden), P570 = 1937-01-01.
